title: Momentum
lede: Why a jab and a cross feel so different, why rolling with a punch saves your jaw, why airbags work, and what happens to a car that hits a truck.

sections.md:
## Momentum
**Momentum** is mass in motion: **p = mv** (unit: kg·m/s). It has direction.

A 36,000 kg truck at 1 m/s has the same momentum as a 1,200 kg car at 30 m/s: **36,000 kg·m/s**. That's why something heavy moving slowly can be just as hard to stop as something light moving fast.

## Impulse: force × time
Changing momentum takes a force applied over time:

**Impulse J = F · Δt = Δp**

For the **same change in momentum**, a **longer** time means a **smaller** force. A shorter time means a **bigger** force.

This one idea explains a lot:
- **Airbags and crumple zones** stretch out the stopping time of your body, cutting the force.
- **Rolling with a punch** (moving your head with it) increases the contact time, reducing the peak force on your jaw and brain.
- **Bending your knees** when landing a jump does the same for your joints.
- A **snapping, stiff** strike shortens contact time with the target, concentrating force.

options: They increase the time of the stop, lowering the force
sections.why: Same Δp, longer Δt, smaller F.

sections.title: Force from stopping time
sections.problem: A 70 kg person moving at 15 m/s is brought to a stop. Compare a 0.01 s stop (hitting a hard surface) with a 0.2 s stop (airbag).
sections.answer: **20× less force** with the airbag. The momentum change was identical; only the time changed.

sections.md:
## Conservation of momentum
In a collision where no outside force acts, **total momentum before = total momentum after**:

**m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = m₁v₁′ + m₂v₂′**

- **Elastic** collisions: objects bounce, and kinetic energy is also conserved (billiard balls come close).
- **Inelastic** collisions: some KE turns into heat, sound and deformation. **Perfectly inelastic**: they stick together.

Momentum is conserved in **both**; kinetic energy only in elastic.

sections.title: Car hits a truck
sections.problem: A 2,000 kg car at 20 m/s rear-ends a 36,000 kg truck stopped at a light. They lock together. How fast do they move just after?
steps: The car's velocity changed by about 19 m/s; the truck's by about 1 m/s.
sections.answer: Same force on each (Newton's third law), but the car's occupants experience about **18 times** the velocity change. In car–truck crashes, physics is brutally unfair to the smaller vehicle.

sections.md:
## Recoil
When a gun fires, the bullet goes forward and the gun kicks back. Before firing, total momentum was zero, so after, it's still zero: **m_bullet × v_bullet = m_gun × v_gun** (in opposite directions). The gun is much heavier, so it moves much slower.

Rockets work the same way: pushing exhaust backward pushes the rocket forward, even in empty space with nothing to push against.

sections.q: Two skaters push apart from rest. The heavier one moves…
sections.why: Equal and opposite momentum: bigger mass, smaller speed.

sections.label: Common traps
sections.md:
- **Momentum is conserved in all collisions** (with no outside forces). Kinetic energy isn't.
- **Direction matters.** Use signs: right +, left −.
- **Equal forces don't mean equal effects.** The lighter object gets the bigger acceleration.
- **Impulse is the change in momentum**, not momentum itself.

A 75 kg fighter's head-and-body system needs a momentum change of 30 kg·m/s from a strike. If the contact time doubles from 0.01 s to 0.02 s, what's the new average force?
practice.why: F = 30 ÷ 0.02 = **1,500 N** (vs 3,000 N at 0.01 s). Doubling the time halves the force.
practice.hint: F = Δp ÷ Δt. (The 75 kg isn't needed.)

practice.q: A 1,500 kg car at 20 m/s collides head-on with a 1,000 kg car at 10 m/s going the opposite way. They stick. Velocity after (in the first car's direction)?
practice.hint: Give the second car's velocity a negative sign.

practice.q: A collision where the objects stick together…
options: conserves both momentum and kinetic energy
conserves momentum but loses kinetic energy
practice.why: Perfectly inelastic: momentum conserved, some KE becomes heat and deformation.
